As someone who has suffered from this for 15 years now, I know firsthand that CFS is real and I believe it has to do with a chronically active autoimmune response. The immune response is energetically expensive, and if it is active for prolonged amounts of time it really drains the bodies energy supply. It is the same lethargic feeling that "normal" people get when they get infected by a virus or bacteria, but the difference is for a normal person the feeling goes away whereas with people with CFS this lethargic feeling is chronic. The main mystery behind CFS is really what are the triggers that can cause your immune system to be overactive (in my case I believe it is triggered by food ingestion activating my immune system).

And yeah, the people claiming it is "psychosomatic" need to knock it off. There is so much in biology that we don't understand, and just to say that the problem only exists in someone's head because you don't currently understand the cause is egotistical, and it certainly is a disservice to patients (such as myself) who turned to these people for help.

The thing is, even if this and similar ailments are psychosomatic (which doesn't seem to be the case here), they are no less deserving of treatment than someone with a cut up limb.
